source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project (IFAD-funded) - "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique" (ផលិតកម្មដំណាំចេកដែលធន់ទៅនឹងការប្រែប្រួលអាកាសធាតុ), November 2018
text:
This booklet, "Climate Resilient Banana Growing Technique," was produced by MAFF's Department of Agricultural Extension under the ASPIRE project (Agriculture Services Programme for Innovation, Resilience and Extension), funded by IFAD, and published November 2018. It targets farmers looking to make banana production more resilient to climate variability - erratic rainfall, heat stress, and wind - through practices such as drip irrigation and bunch bagging, alongside standard cultivation steps.

Banana is highlighted as a fruit crop that produces bunches with many hands and is a good source of vitamins and minerals as part of a balanced diet, and one that Cambodian smallholders are well positioned to grow given the crop's relatively short cycle to first harvest.
